sources_considered.why: Read the quarterly growth discussion. It provides counter-context but cannot represent the industry in the selected month.
Read the Ramp analysis. It measures April business adoption, not May spending growth or realized industry revenue.
Read the company announcement. A single company's run rate and funding do not settle industry commercial deceleration.

evidence_items.publisher: Anthropic, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence_items.locator: Business discussion of Opus 4.5, immediately after the quarterly revenue-growth comparison
evidence_items.explanation: The filing describes accelerating quarterly revenue growth and attributes it to several commercial and product factors. It is material counter-context, but an earlier result from one company cannot settle the broader May claim.

unresolved_gaps: No representative May enterprise-spending growth series was established.
No matched industry revenue series establishes commercial deceleration during May.
The source leaves the meaning of 'AI is slowing down' broader than any single commercial measure.
The cited cost concerns are not quantified as a contribution to aggregate growth.
